title: Verdicts vary
statement: The same marker can give different verdicts on the same answer: send each test answer more than once, and re-send every known miss after each rebuild.
detail:
In the marking test, 9 of 10 answers sent three times got the same verdict each time, and one right answer met a
criterion in 3 of 4 calls; a second marker accepted 14 of 15 right answers in one run and 15 of 15 seven minutes later

came back, one timed out twice and one got half credit (`g9/review/2026-10-08-lesson1-build-map/README.md`).
against: the second marker's verdicts on 8 repeated answers were the same in both runs. A later run found counter-evidence (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/MEMORY.md`).

LLM-as-judge is non-deterministic at any temperature > 0 OR even at temp=0 (small variance from server-side batching, KV-cache timing, random sampling fallback paths). Single-call evaluation is unreliable.

Video scripts use a single LLM pass with binary pass/fail metrics. Running at temperature=1.0 (the default evaluator config) adds noise without a consensus loop to cancel it out, causing the same script to flip between SUPERIOR and INFERIOR across runs.

The 0.99 threshold over ~82 non-error items tolerates ZERO failures. With LLM judge nondeterminism flipping 1-3 verdicts per run, this gate is structurally unsatisfiable and blocks valid PRs indefinitely.
